NO. 035 · Wetlands & Waterways / Rallidae · Rails & Crakes

Eurasian Coot

白骨顶 · bái gǔ dǐng Fulica atra
Winter visitor Common 36–42 cm Protected (China) IUCN LC

A 'black duck' with a slab of bone on its forehead

All sooty black, with a snow-white plate set into the forehead — as if someone had knocked it there. It is not a duck but a close relative of the rails: the toes are lobed, and it walks with a roll.

Gallery

One scientific illustration for shape and colour blocks, two field photographs for how it looks in real light. Click any image to enlarge.

Identification

  • Frontal shieldA white bony shield on the forehead running down to the base of the bill — the most striking feature of the species.
  • PlumageSlate-black to dark grey throughout, slightly darker on the back and paler below; plumage dense and waterproof.
  • BillWhite to pale pinkish-white with a slightly darker tip, in sharp contrast with the black body.
  • FeetLegs grey-green, the toes with lateral lobes — not the full web of a duck — good for both swimming and diving.

Behaviour

A bird of open water, swimming and diving well and usually diving to escape. It feeds on aquatic plants, algae and a little animal matter. In winter it gathers on South China reservoirs and lakes in flocks of tens to a hundred or more. It needs a running start across the surface to take off, pattering along with its feet.

Voice

A short, loud 'kup' or 'kowk', audible at night; flocks also give low mutterings and metallic trills.

Where to find it in Zhuhai

  • Qianwu Reservoir
  • Xiangshan Lake Park
  • Dajingshan Reservoir
  • Doumen fish ponds
Field note
Separating it from Common Moorhen: Coot has a white shield, is black throughout and has lobed toes; Moorhen has a red shield, a white line along the flank and a red ring on the leg.
